planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to filtered sun; the chartreuse-gold color of 'Ogon' holds best out of intense midday exposure, which can bleach or scorch the foliage.

directions: 'Ogon' is a slow-growing sport of holly osmanthus prized for its consistently bright chartreuse-to-golden-yellow foliage, a color that persists year-round rather than fading to green like many variegated shrubs. The small, spiny-toothed leaves hold their glow best in bright, filtered shade, where the shrub becomes a strong color accent against darker-leaved evergreens in a woodland border. Small, sweetly fragrant white flowers appear tucked among the leaves in fall, though the plant is grown primarily for foliage rather than bloom. Site in humus-rich, well-drained soil sheltered from harsh afternoon sun and drying winter wind, and prune lightly in spring only to maintain shape.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to morning sun; this older, larger-growing variegated selection tolerates more shade than gold-centered forms without losing its cream-yellow leaf margins.

directions: Among the oldest variegated holly osmanthus selections still widely grown, 'Aureomarginatus' carries dark green, spine-toothed leaves edged in a broad, creamy-yellow margin that brightens shaded corners without the more dramatic color shifts of newer cultivars. It grows into a larger, denser shrub than many compact modern selections, making it useful as a substantial screen or background planting rather than a small accent. Inconspicuous but sweetly fragrant white flowers open along the stems in autumn, perfuming the surrounding air well before they are visually noticed. Grow in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to filtered morning sun, and prune after flowering if a tighter form is wanted.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (Bean's Trees and Shrubs)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; the small, mostly spineless leaves make this a good low-hedge substitute for boxwood in shaded gardens.

directions: 'Myrtifolius' is a dense, slow-growing dwarf form of holly osmanthus with small, narrow, mostly smooth-edged leaves that lack the sharp spines typical of the species, giving it a fine, refined texture reminiscent of true myrtle. Its naturally compact, rounded habit and tolerance of shearing make it a popular choice for low formal hedges or edging in shaded gardens where clipped boxwood struggles with disease. Small, hidden white flowers in fall carry the same sweet fragrance typical of the genus, though the plant's main appeal is its fine-textured, low-maintenance foliage. Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to sun, and shear in spring or after flowering to maintain a tight form.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (Bean's Trees and Shrubs)

common_name: San Jose Osmanthus (Compact Hybrid Fragrant Tea Olive)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; 'San Jose' is a long-established Southern nursery selection widely used as a dense, fragrant screening hedge.

directions: 'San Jose' is a vigorous fortunei hybrid selection grown widely across the Southeast as a large, dense evergreen screen or hedge, valued for its glossy, leathery, gently toothed leaves and heavy fall bloom. Clusters of small cream-white flowers open in autumn with a strong, sweet apricot-like fragrance that carries well beyond the planting, distinguishing it from purely ornamental-foliage osmanthus cultivars. Its faster growth and larger eventual size than compact heterophyllus selections make it better suited to boundary plantings and tall privacy screens than small foundation beds. Grow in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun, and prune after the fall flowers finish if a more formal hedge shape is desired.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; named for the historic Fruitland Nurseries of Augusta, Georgia, this older fortunei selection grows into a large, dense specimen given room to mature.

directions: 'Fruitlandii' is a broad, rounded fortunei hybrid selection tracing back to the historic Fruitland Nurseries in Augusta, Georgia, prized in older Southern landscapes for its dense, holly-textured evergreen foliage and heavy autumn flowering. Small tubular cream flowers cluster along the stems in fall and fill the surrounding air with a strong, sweet apricot fragrance detectable well before the shrub is seen. It matures into one of the larger fortunei-type osmanthus selections, so it performs best as a specimen or tall background planting rather than a tight foundation shrub. Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun, and prune only lightly to control size after the fall bloom period.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to part shade; 'Compacta' stays denser and shorter than the arching wild species, needing less room in a small shaded bed.

directions: 'Compacta' is a tighter, denser-growing selection of native drooping leucothoe that keeps the species' glossy, leathery leaves and gracefully arching stems on a noticeably smaller, more mounded frame. Short racemes of small, fragrant, white urn-shaped flowers dangle beneath the branches in late spring, followed by good burgundy-purple winter foliage color typical of the species. Its reduced size and slower spread suit it to smaller shaded foundation plantings or woodland edges where full-size drooping leucothoe would eventually crowd the space. Grow in consistently moist, strongly acidic soil in shade to part shade, sheltered from winter wind and hot afternoon sun.

common_name: Royal Ruby Leucothoe (Dwarf Red-New-Growth Keiske's Doghobble)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in moist, humus-rich, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; 'Royal Ruby' is a selected dwarf clone of Leucothoe keiskei chosen for especially deep red new growth on a low, spreading frame.

directions: 'Royal Ruby' is a low, slow-spreading selection of the dwarf Japanese species Leucothoe keiskei, chosen for shoots that emerge a deep, glossy ruby-red before settling into narrow, dark green leaves that flush red again through the cold months. Its diminutive height keeps it well below the arching mounds of drooping and coast leucothoe, making it a good textural groundcover or edging plant along a shaded path or rock garden. Nodding, pure-white, cylindrical flowers appear in short clusters in midsummer, larger individually than the flowers of most other cultivated leucothoes. Grow in consistently moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade sheltered from hot afternoon sun and drying wind, and mulch to keep the shallow roots cool and evenly moist.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (Bean's Trees and Shrubs)
